summary: Stuart H. Blackburn is an Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University and the University of California, Berkeley. He held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1991 to 2011.

Stuart Piggott (1910–1996) was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He studied at Churcher's College and University College London's Institute of Archaeology (c. 1934–1936), and held a post at the University of Edinburgh from 1946 to 1977.
Stuart Ray Sarbacker works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001, where he studied under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe.

Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) was a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Chulalongkorn University, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and UCL. He served as professor and rector at Silpakorn University and president of the Siam Society.

Subhash Kak (born 1947) works in Indology and computational fields. He studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under Pavaguda V. Indiresan. His career includes professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and Oklahoma State University (2007).

Subrata K. Mitra (born 1949) studied at Utkal University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Rochester. He held academic posts at the University of Hull, University of Nottingham, Heidelberg University (c. 1994–2014), and National University of Singapore.

Sucheng Chan (born 1941) is a historian who studied at Swarthmore College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and UC Berkeley. She served as an emerita professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara from circa 1988 to 2005.
Sudan Shakya is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held a post as a professor at Shuchiin University, attested between 2013 and 2017 as well as in 2026.

Sudhakara Dvivedi (1855–1910) was an Indologist who studied under Devakṛṣṇa. He succeeded Bapu Deva Sastri in 1889 and served as librarian, professor, and head of the mathematics faculty at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1883 to circa 1905.

Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Gujarat University, University of Mannheim, and University of Vienna. He held positions at Harvard, IIM Ahmedabad, and IIT Delhi, alongside numerous international visiting professorships.

Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and held a post at King's College London attested in 2001–2003.

Suhasini D. Laddu (born 1926) is an Indologist and linguist. She was affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1968) and served as Editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).
Sujeet Kumar works in computational fields and Indology. He has held academic posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur and B.P. Mandal College of Engineering.

Suk Fun Ng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014). Ng studied under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, and teacher K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sukhlal Sanghvi (1880–1978) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at Shri Yashovijaya Jain Sanskrit Pathshala and under Balakrishna Mishra, later holding posts at Gujarat Vidyapith and as Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University.

Sukumar Sen (1900–1992) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala. He served as lecturer and Khaira Professor at the University of Calcutta.

Sukumari Bhattacharji (1921–2014) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University, and held teaching posts at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and Jadavpur University (1957–1986).
Sulagna Bhattacharya is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Pratap Bandyopadhyay. She holds an H P Shastri Research Fellowship at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Sulak Sivaraksa (born 1933) is an author and activist in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Assumption College, Bangkok, and the University of Wales Lampeter, and held visiting posts at Berkeley, Harvard, Cornell, and Toronto.

Sumathi Ramaswamy (born 1961) is a historian and Indologist. She studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania, and held faculty positions at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Michigan.
